arxiv-2006-01938.title: Nurse is Closer to Woman than Surgeon? Mitigating Gender-Biased Proximities in Word Embeddings
arxiv-2006-01938.creator: Vaibhav Kumar 1, Tenzin Singhay Bhotia 1, Vaibhav Kumar 1, Tanmoy Chakraborty 2
arxiv-2006-01938.description: Abstract Word embeddings are the standard model for semantic and syntactic representations of words. Unfortunately, these models have been shown to exhibit undesirable word associations resulting from gender, racial, and religious biases. Existing post-processing methods for debiasing word embeddings are unable to mitigate gender bias hidden in the spatial arrangement of word vectors.

arxiv-2102-08002.title: Reversible Random Walks on Dynamic Graphs
arxiv-2102-08002.creator: Nobutaka Shimizu, Takeharu Shiraga
arxiv-2102-08002.description: A 2021 arXiv research paper by Nobutaka Shimizu, Takeharu Shiraga. Recently, random walks on dynamic graphs have been studied because of their adaptivity to the time-varying structure of real-world networks. In general, there is a tremendous gap between static and dynamic graph settings for the lazy simple random walk: Although O ⁡ ( n 3 ) O(n^{3}) cover time was shown for any static graphs of n n vertices, there is an edge-changing dynamic graph with an exponential hitting time.

arxiv-2110-12776.title: Clustering matrices through optimal permutations
arxiv-2110-12776.creator: Flaviano Morone
arxiv-2110-12776.description: Abstract Matrices are two-dimensional data structures allowing one to conceptually organize information golub . For example, adjacency matrices are useful to store the links of a network; correlation matrices are simple ways to arrange gene co-expression data or correlations of neuronal activities patrik ; zimmer .

arxiv-2111-05492.title: μ \mu SR study of unconventional pairing symmetry in the quasi-1D Na 2 Cr 3 As 3 superconductor
arxiv-2111-05492.creator: A Bhattacharyya, D T Adroja, Y Feng, Debarchan Das, P K Biswas, Tanmoy Das, J. Zhao
arxiv-2111-05492.description: Abstract We report the finding of a novel pairing state in a newly discovered superconductor Na 2 Cr 3 As 3 . This material has a noncentrosymmetric quasi-one-dimensional crystal structure and is superconducting at T C ∼ T_{\mathrm{C}}\sim 8.0 K.

arxiv-2304-01777.title: On the distribution of subset sums of certain sets in ℤ p 2 \mathbb{Z}^{2}_{p}
arxiv-2304-01777.creator: Norbert Hegyvári
arxiv-2304-01777.description: Abstract . A given subset A A of natural numbers is said to be complete if every element of ℕ \mathbb{N} is the sum of distinct terms taken from A A . This topic is strongly connected to the knapsack problem which is known to be NP complete.

arxiv-2308-01575.title: Quasinormal modes of the spherical bumblebee black holes with a global monopole
arxiv-2308-01575.creator: Rui-Hui Lin, Rui Jiang, Xiang-Hua Zhai
arxiv-2308-01575.description: Abstract The bumblebee model is an extension of the Einstein-Maxwell theory that allows for the spontaneous breaking of the Lorentz symmetry of the spacetime. In this paper, we study the quasinormal modes of the spherical black holes in this model that are characterized by a global monopole.

D 97 (2018) 034503 , JHEP 2017 (2017) 62 ], relates the factorial growth of a perturbative series (in QCD) to the power p p of a power correction Λ p / Q p \Lambda^{p}/Q^{p} . arxiv-2312-03907.creator: Julia Xénelkis de Hénon

arxiv-2406-17713.title: Multi-objective Binary Differential Approach with Parameter Tuning for Discovering Business Process Models: MoD-ProM
arxiv-2406-17713.creator: A. Sonia Deshmukh 1, B. Shikha Gupta 2, C. Naveen Kumar 3
arxiv-2406-17713.description: Abstract Process discovery approaches analyze the business data to automatically uncover structured information, known as a process model. The quality of a process model is measured using quality dimensions- completeness (replay fitness), preciseness, simplicity, and generalization. Traditional process discovery algorithms usually output a single process model.

arxiv-2411-07378.title: Data-Driven Analysis of AI in Medical Device Software in China: Trends of Deep Learning and Traditional AI Based on Regulatory Data
arxiv-2411-07378.creator: Yu Han, Aaron Ceross, Sarim Ather, Jeroen H.M. Bergmann
arxiv-2411-07378.description: Abstract Artificial intelligence (AI) in medical device software (MDSW) represents a transformative clinical technology, attracting increasing attention within both the medical community and the regulators. In this study, we leverage a data-driven approach to automatically extract and analyze AI-enabled medical devices (AIMD) from the National Medical Products Administration (NMPA) regulatory database.

arxiv-2509-23183.title: ZeroSiam: An Efficient Siamese for Test-Time Entropy Optimization without Collapse
arxiv-2509-23183.creator: Guohao Chen, Shuaicheng Niu, Deyu Chen, Jiahao Yang, Zitian Zhang, Mingkui Tan, Pengcheng Wu, Zhiqi Shen {guohao.chen, shuaicheng.niu, zqshen}@ntu.edu.sg, Nanyang Technological University South China University of Technology
arxiv-2509-23183.description: A 2025 arXiv research paper by Guohao Chen, Shuaicheng Niu, Deyu Chen, Jiahao Yang, Zitian Zhang, Mingkui Tan, Pengcheng Wu, Zhiqi Shen {guohao.chen, shuaicheng.niu, zqshen}@ntu.edu.sg, Nanyang Technological University South China University of Technology. Test-time entropy minimization helps adapt a model to novel environments and incentivize its reasoning capability, unleashing the model’s potential during inference by allowing it to evolve and improve in real-time using its own predictions, achieving promising performance.

arxiv-2511-04671.title: X-Diffusion : Training Diffusion Policies on Cross-Embodiment Human Demonstrations
arxiv-2511-04671.creator: Maximus A. Pace, Prithwish DanChuanruo NingAtiksh BhardwajAudrey DuEdward W. Duan, Wei-Chiu Ma, Kushal KediaCornell University https://portal-cornell.github.io/X-Diffusion/
arxiv-2511-04671.description: Abstract Human videos can be recorded quickly and at scale, making them an appealing source of training data for robot learning. However, humans and robots differ fundamentally in embodiment, resulting in mismatched action execution. Direct kinematic retargeting of human hand motion can therefore produce actions that are physically infeasible for robots.

arxiv-2602-22117.title: Loss mechanisms in high-coherence multimode mechanical resonators coupled to superconducting circuits
arxiv-2602-22117.creator: Raquel Garcia-Belles, Alexander Anferov, Lukas F. Deeg, Loris Colicchio, Arianne Brooks, Tom Schatteburg, Maxwell Drimmer, Ines C. arxiv-2602-22117.description: Abstract Circuit quantum acoustodynamics (cQAD) devices have a wide range of applications in quantum science, all of which depend crucially on the quantum coherence of the mechanical subsystem. In this context, high-overtone bulk acoustic-wave resonators (HBARs) are particularly promising, since they have shown very high quality factors with negligible dephasing.

pmc-11506049.description: The epidermis of the skin and skin appendages, such as nails, hair and sebaceous glands, depend on a balance of cell proliferation and terminal differentiation in order to fulfill their functions at the interface of the body and the environment.

pmc-11638647.title: The effects of alpha-lipoic acid transdermal patch for local subcutaneous fat reduction: A randomized, placebo-controlled, clinical trial in overweight volunteers
pmc-11638647.creator: Kanidta Sooklert, Sasin Thamakaison, Siwaporn Nilyai, Sarocha Cherdchom, Rojrit Rojanathanes, Amornpun Sereemaspun
pmc-11638647.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2024). BackgroundCombating obesity is challenging, as anti-obesity compounds lose effectiveness or cause severe side effects when delivered via conventional routes. Thus, there is a need for new, effective treatment routes that are home-based and safe for long-term use. This double-blind, placebo-controlled clinical trial aimed to investigate the efficacy of a biocellulose transdermal patch containing α-lipoic acid (ALA), an anti-obesity compound, in reducing subcutaneous fat accumulation.MethodsOne hundred and sixteen overweight participants (average age 37.96 ± 7.80 years) were recruited for the study.

pmc-13275189.title: A Case of Painful Legs and Moving Toes Syndrome Mimicking Restless Legs Syndrome
pmc-13275189.creator: Yu Li, Risa Maeda, Yoshihide Okano, Tetsuya Kanai, Takanori Uehara
pmc-13275189.description: A peer-reviewed research article from Europe PMC (2026). Painful legs and moving toes syndrome (PLMT) is a neurological disorder characterized by leg pain accompanied by involuntary toe movements. It may be misdiagnosed as restless legs syndrome (RLS) due to overlapping clinical features. We report the case of a 69-year-old woman with a seven-year history of pain involving all toes of both feet that improved with standing or walking and worsened when lying down. She had no sleep disturbance and was unaware of involuntary movements.

pmc-13300685.title: A novel pace mapping parameter to predict procedural success of left bundle branch area pacing: Lead II/III Discordance Index
pmc-13300685.creator: B Hunuk, F Besiroglu, O Cagac, H Altay, O Kozan
pmc-13300685.description: BackgroundLeft-bundle-branch-area-pacing (LBBAP) has developed as a physiological pacing alternative, however optimal techniques still need to be elucidated. Pace-mapping the interventricular septum for the optimal septal penetration site, targeting DII/DIII discordance and a notch at the nadir of V1-QRS has been suggested in consensus papers.

pmc-13355386.title: Comparison of Measurement Techniques for Photoreceptor Loss in Geographic Atrophy
pmc-13355386.creator: Maria Schulz, Nathan Macha, Sairi Zhang, Jeong W. Pak, Shelby Storm, David Alvaro Lopez, Barbara A. Blodi, Amitha Domalpally
pmc-13355386.description: PurposeEllipsoid zone (EZ) loss is an emerging end point in geographic atrophy (GA) clinical trials. Standardized ground truth is important to train artificial intelligence models in this biomarker. This study compares segmentation and edge detection methods for quantifying EZ and retinal pigment epithelium (RPE) loss on optical coherence tomography (OCT).

pmc-13478489.title: Structural insights into predicted protein–protein interactions and protein complexes in the human proteome
pmc-13478489.creator: Jimin Pei, Jing Zhang, Qian Cong
pmc-13478489.description: Large-scale computational predictions of human protein-protein interactions (PPIs) have recently enabled systematic mapping of the human interactome at near-atomic resolution. In our previous work, we reported nearly 18,000 high-confidence predicted PPIs, along with selected examples that demonstrated the ability of these predictions to reveal both pairwise associations across diverse pathways and multi-subunit complex organization.
